advice: Abstain from a new scratch-stride proposal. The earlier 320-byte stride proposal has no supplied measured outcome, but the swarm-selected 272-byte padded layout was measured and rejected; proposing another padding variant now would need a distinct ranked selection. The supplied evidence also gives cache line and L1D sizes but no cache-set indexing or associativity data, so it does not support choosing a useful stride. Keep the current 256-byte stride unless a distinct layout is selected for review. For any future padding experiment, state the exact allocation and consumer offsets, then measure the full timed call—including allocation, packing traffic, and cleanup—with ten reports and ten fresh alternating paired controls; preserve the fixed correctness, promotion, and held-out gates.
risks: No cache-conflict benefit is established. Padding may increase scratch footprint and traffic, and a changed stride or rewind can cause out-of-bounds access or incorrect results. The prior jointly measured TRANS_B result does not test this scratch layout and cannot be attributed to this advisor.
